extractedItems.title: Taking relief from abnormal course conditions in a bunker
extractedItems.question: Your ball is in a bunker and a puddle interferes with your stance. What are your options for taking relief?

choices.text: Drop within one club-length in the bunker with no penalty
Drop outside the bunker with no penalty
Drop outside the bunker, but take a one-stroke penalty
Play the ball as it lies with no penalty

extractedItems.explanation: You may drop within the bunker without penalty or drop outside the bunker for a one-stroke penalty.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage girl golfer in a bunker with a puddle, preparing to drop a ball within the bunker to take relief.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Teenage girl golfer dropping a ball in a bunker with a puddle.

extractedItems.title: Dropping outside a bunker due to abnormal conditions
extractedItems.question: What must you do if you decide to take relief outside the bunker from abnormal course conditions in the bunker?

choices.text: Drop outside the bunker with no penalty
Drop outside the bunker but add one penalty stroke
Place the ball anywhere outside the bunker with no penalty
You cannot take relief outside the bunker

extractedItems.explanation: If you take relief outside the bunker for abnormal course conditions, you must add one penalty stroke.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage boy golfer standing just outside a bunker after dropping a ball, taking a penalty stroke for relief.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Teenage boy golfer dropping a ball outside a bunker for a penalty.

extractedItems.title: Animal holes and relief
extractedItems.question: Which of these is classed as an animal hole for relief?

choices.text: A hole dug by a rabbit
A shoe print from a previous player
A sprinkler head
A footprint from a bird

extractedItems.explanation: Only a hole dug by an animal (like a rabbit) counts as an animal hole. A footprint or a sprinkler head does not.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teen girl golfer standing next to her ball in a bunker, looking at a small animal hole nearby.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Teenage girl golfer checks a ball near an animal hole in the bunker.

extractedItems.title: If the bunker is completely flooded
extractedItems.question: What happens if your ball is in a bunker that is completely flooded with water and you can't find any dry spot to drop the ball in the bunker?

choices.text: You must play from the water with no penalty
You take free relief outside the bunker
You must drop outside the bunker and add one penalty stroke
You can choose any spot on the course for free

extractedItems.explanation: If the bunker is completely flooded, you may drop outside the bunker but you must take one penalty stroke.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage boy golfer looking at a bunker that is totally filled with water, preparing to drop a ball outside the bunker.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Teenage boy golfer dropping a ball outside a flooded bunker.
